data.title: Role of Autophagy in Scleral Remodeling During Form-Deprivation Myopia
data.authors: Wen J; Tang S; Zhang Xiaoxiao

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Excess scleral autophagy links hypoxic stress to extracellular matrix remodelling in experimental myopia. In form-deprived guinea pigs, subconjunctival rapamycin made myopia worse and 3-MA alleviated it, while atropine slowed myopia and suppressed autophagy-related changes. AMPK/mTOR/P70S6K signalling was measured, but the paper does not establish it as the mediating route.
data.abstract_excerpt: Autophagy has been implicated in tissue remodeling, but its role in scleral remodeling during myopia development and in atropine-mediated myopia control remains unclear. We investigated this issue using complementary in vitro and in vivo models. Human scleral fibroblasts (HSFs) were exposed to hypoxia and treated with rapamycin (RAPA) or 3-methyladenine (3-MA). Beclin-1 knockdown and bafilomycin A1 (BafA1)-based LC3B II accumulation assays were used to assess the functional contribution of autophagy and autophagic flux.

extracted_findings.effect: Excess mTOR-regulated scleral autophagy promotes myopia: rapamycin worsened it, 3-MA reduced it; atropine's benefit involved suppressing autophagy
